claims.text: Calling toString on an Output<T> in Pulumi produces placeholder text like `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` in logs, generated files, or resource properties instead of the actual value.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ titled 'Output value errors' that covers this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
A Pulumi docs troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading an output value like a plain value.
Pulumi Cloud returns the error '409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress' when an update conflicts with an in-progress update.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors.
On Apple Silicon Macs, x86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2 can cause crashes or hangs.
The Pulumi CLI produces a `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` error when it cannot access a self-managed (DIY) state backend, documented at the using-a-diy-backend page.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi supports limiting operations to specific resources with `--target` and `--exclude` flags.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
Pulumi provides automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging.
Pulumi dev builds are pre-release builds providing bug fixes not yet shipped in a stable release.
Pulumi offers paid support options.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the providing resource has been created or updated.

Converting a Pulumi Output to a string directly (instead of via apply or an equivalent helper) does not raise an error by default; Pulumi silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In TypeScript, the string produced by converting an Output via toString contains text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use apply or pulumi.interpolate.
In TypeScript, calling JSON.stringify() on an Output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Python, converting an Output to a string produces text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported` and Pulumi also logs a warning; no exception is raised.
In Python, passing an Output to json.dumps() fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; Output.json_dumps() should be used instead.
In Go, passing a pulumi.StringOutput where a string is expected is a compile error.
In C#, converting an Output via ToString produces text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use Apply or Output.Format.

Setting the environment variable PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true (supported in TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes converting an Output to a string throw an exception instead of returning placeholder text.

The string-composition helpers are pulumi.interpolate and pulumi.concat in TypeScript, Output.concat/Output.format/Output.json_dumps in Python, pulumi.Sprintf/pulumi.JSONMarshal in Go, and Output.Format in C#.
An apply callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished running.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values; a resource's logical name is one position that cannot accept an output.

In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on a Pulumi Output is generally always true because the Output object itself is evaluated; in a statically typed language it is usually a compile error because Output<bool> is not a bool.
Values known when the program starts, such as stack configuration read with pulumi.Config, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values that can be branched on normally.
Passing an Output as a resource logical name or loop bound fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using an Output as a loop bound (range(some_output)) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise; it silently keys on the Output object itself.

Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously read a resolved value from an Output; awaiting or synchronously reading an Output fails to compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. `res.Outputs` in Go).
The cross-referenced pages exist: /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/ (#outputs), /apply/, /all/, /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, and /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
